newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says Russia to defend Ukraine in crisis.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says Russia to defend Ukraine in crisis.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, who arrived in Kiev on Friday to sign a pact on bilateral relations, said before leaving that Moscow would defend Ukraine "in extreme situations".
"This is in the agreement, that we will participate together to defend Ukraine if anything happens," Yeltsin said in an interview broadcast on Friday on Russian public television.
Yeltsin did not specify the conditions under which Russia would come to the aid of its fellow ex-Soviet republic.

In the interview, he discussed an accord between Moscow and Kiev dividing the Soviet Black Sea Fleet, over which the two sides had squabbled for years, and allowing Russia to lease naval facilities at the Ukrainian port of Sevastopol.
"I am in favour of us jointly providing security and helping each other in extreme situations so it is obligatory to help," Yeltsin said.

Russia has mutual defence agreements with most members of the Commonwealth of Independent States but not Ukraine, Moldova and Turkmenistan. The CIS groups the former Soviet republics except for the Baltic states.
Yeltsin's statement came three days after he signed an agreement with NATO establishing a new security relationship.

The Kremlin leader, who is anxious to prevent former Soviet states from joining NATO, also repeated his warning that Russia would rethink relations with the Western alliance if it sought to expand into the ex-Soviet republics.
"Of course NATO will be discussed," Yeltsin said about his planned talks with Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma.

"We will reconfirm what I said: if they (NATO leaders) try to drag one of the (ex-Soviet) republics into their sphere as members of NATO, we will re-evaluate our relationship with the alliance," he said. "I've made that clear and can repeat it."

Yeltsin said the Russia-Ukraine agreement will encompass a wide variety of issues including transport, education and energy, and seek to reduce tensions that have evolved between the two Slav nations since the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991.
He also said he would propose creating a customs union with Ukraine.
